chapter: Hotels, Mardi Gras and the Gulf Coast
title: Fishing, crabbing and shrimping on the coast
summary: Julius recalls walking the sand beds for crabs, his father's shrimp nets, torch fishing and mullets.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, I wish I could have been a part of some of those days. Yes. I came up in the wrong generation. I'd like to...

I was saying the other day, I wish I had, uh, some of the, uh, and I like, used to get so much good fish over there. Now, this water began to, you know, gather in this and do this and do that. And you can't get all that now. The crabs, you can't get that. The shrimp, you can't get all that. And, uh, Sylvester Cap and I, we used to walk out to, like, from here to Claiborne Street. In between, they'd have that, uh, they'd have the, what you call it? Uh, they'd have the, the sand beds. The what? Sand beds, they used to call it. Sand beds. In other words, like, you could walk from here to here. Oh, I was just saying. Right. And they wouldn't have it and they'd have sand here, you see. Right. And you'd get ready to walk from here, it would be water about up to your ankle, maybe to your knee, and over there it would be sand. You could keep on walking around. Yeah, uh-huh, well in between there, they used to have crabs like that.
Just walk along and, uh, we'd take sticks and catch them. And, uh, sometimes Calc and Sylvester would come home with a whole cycle.
Toes work just as well, too. Uh-huh. Toes work just as well.

Yeah, uh-huh, right. And, uh, it was so wonderful. And I liked shrimp. You could walk over there. Over there you could walk out there and pick up, uh, my daddy used to walk from water up to here. And they had a little net. He used to make those nets. And throw out there and shoot, he'd come back with a whole big, half a sack of shrimp, and great big shrimp.
Uh-huh, uh-huh. And at night, my daddy used to go clowning.
With a torchlight and a spear.
And you see big clowners like that, big clowners like that. I used to see—
Well, you still see kids doing that during the night.

Yeah, I used to ask my daddy to let me, uh, I said, let me get it. Boy, that thing will drown you in that water. He said, you hit him down, you hit him with that spear, you wouldn't be heavy enough to hold him. And he'd get out from underneath there. And, uh, that's good eating. This clowners.
Listen, I don't want to pay you for this. So let me get this, uh, thing. You might want to read this over before you sign in there, ain't?
I used to be crazy about those, uh, mullets over there.
The what? Mullets. Mullets. Mullets? Mm-hmm. You know that not many people are, but the ones that live over there, uh, never lose that taste of the little small mullets.
